mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 6.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or Rank IC is negative over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based demand contraction that signals an imminent recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In supply chain disruption regimes (INDPRO < 105.0), manufacturing bottlenecks increase input costs and reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation that prompts Federal Reserve tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC is negative over any 6-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior month indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 annual growth > 2.0%), strong consumer demand (RSAFS) drives corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth exceeds 2.0%, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a broad-based supply shock that increases input costs and reduces economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 6-month rolling window.
